acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each handler uses a named Admin capability, platform principal, or explicitly registered non-user principal.
evidence: PREMISE THAT WAS WRONG, corrected before any edit: none of the three handlers used `withAdminAuth`. All three were bare exported functions, which the ADMIN-016 analyzer classes `no_route_guard`, and they were THREE OF THE FOUR members of the pinned `noSourceGuardMethods` set. The dispatch text said they 'currently run on an implicit principal - withAdminAuth, which supplies only { user, supabase }'; the truth is that two of them (the invite validation and the job posting) authenticated nobody at all, and the third authenticated through getAuthenticatedUserId in lib/api/hiring-route-helpers.ts. `withAdminAuth` supplying no organization is therefore not why this task existed. ADMIN-027 was the right reference for the shape of the fix, not for the diagnosis.

PATCH /api/admin/onboarding/documents/[documentId]/review -> named capability `hiring.manage`, enforced by withAdminCapability at app/api/admin/onboarding/documents/[documentId]/review/route.ts:56. `hiring.manage` is in the ADMIN_CAPABILITIES catalog (lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:22) and is the capability that names this action; the registry previously claimed `tour.view`, which the route has never enforced.

GET /api/admin/onboarding/enhanced-invite -> explicitly registered non-user principal. authClass is now `public_share_token`, which is one of the seven classes the proof test's 'declares an explicit capability or an explicit non-capability principal for every method' test accepts as a real principal rather than a permissive gap. The principal is the invitation share token: the caller is an invitee who has not signed up, and app/onboarding/enhanced-onboarding-flow/page.tsx:114 is the only consumer.

POST /api/admin/staffing/job-postings -> named capability `workforce.manage`, enforced by withAdminCapability at app/api/admin/staffing/job-postings/route.ts:19. The route previously had no guard of its own; the only authorization was inside the `createJobPosting` server action it delegates to.

The analyzer agrees, measured rather than asserted: guardClass is `capability_gated` with gateCapabilities ['hiring.manage'] for the review route and ['workforce.manage'] for the postings route, read from the real source through __tests__/admin/support/admin-route-guard-proof.ts.

NEGATIVE CONTROL A2 - the two named gates can fail. Route A's gate was replaced with the ADMIN-027 shape (withAuth + resolveActingAdminContext, acting context but NO capability gate) and the suite went red: 'AssertionError: expected 200 to be 403' on 'refuses a user who may manage hiring for the employer but does not hold hiring.manage'. That user holds a real canManageHiring grant for the employer and a `ticketing` role, so with the gate removed they were served the review and the document was approved. Route C's gate was removed the same way and the suite went red on 'expected undefined to be capability_denied'. Both reverted byte-exactly.

FUNCTIONAL NARROWING, recorded rather than hidden. `hiring.manage` is deliberately excluded from PRODUCTION_CAPABILITIES (lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:88-90 excludes tour.archive, tour.publish and hiring.manage from the production/tour-manager bundle), so the review route is now reachable by owner/admin acting contexts rather than by any actor with canManageHiring on the employer. That is the truthful capability for a hiring-compliance review, and the previous posture was strictly wider because the route had no Admin gate at all - but it IS a behaviour change on two live callers (components/hiring/hiring-onboarding-panel.tsx:74 and components/hiring/onboarding-kanban.tsx:140). If the product wants production managers to review onboarding documents, that is an RBAC catalog decision in lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts, which is outside this working set. Not fixed here, deliberately.

No principal was invented to make a figure move. `public_share_token` for the invite route is the honest classification and it costs +1 on nonSourceComparableClasses; a cheaper 'keep it legacy_pending_migration' reading was rejected because legacy_pending_migration is an admitted gap, not a principal, and AC-1 asks for a registered one.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each route contract declares a source-proven resource boundary.
evidence: All three entries in lib/admin/route-registry/workforce.ts move from `{ kind: 'none_recorded', boundBy: [], verifiedAt: '' }` to a declared boundary, and in each case the `verifiedAt` marker is a literal that exists in the route file, which is what proveAdminRouteEntry checks (`analysis.markers[boundary.kind].includes(boundary.verifiedAt)`).

PATCH /api/admin/onboarding/documents/[documentId]/review -> `{ kind: 'organization_entity', boundBy: ['resolveHiringEntity('], verifiedAt: 'resolveHiringEntity(' }`. The marker is the call that authorizes the caller-named employer in the route (route.ts:70-76), not a comment and not a token that only exists in the registry. `/api/admin/applications/[id]/audit` in the same fragment already declares `organization_entity` for the sibling hiring command, so the shape is the fragment's own.

GET /api/admin/onboarding/enhanced-invite -> `{ kind: 'public_share', boundBy: ['shareToken'], verifiedAt: 'shareToken' }`. The route now names its credential `shareToken` (route.ts:19) and it is the only thing that selects the single candidate row the route discloses. This is the weakest of the three and is recorded as such: the `public_share` marker table in the analyzer is only ['shareToken', 'share_token'], so `boundBy` cannot name anything richer without inventing a token the route does not use.

POST /api/admin/staffing/job-postings -> `{ kind: 'organization_entity', boundBy: ['hasEntityPermission('], verifiedAt: 'hasEntityPermission(' }`. The venue is named by the caller and authorized server-side in the route before the action is reached (route.ts:26-36). `/api/admin/staffing/performance` in the same fragment already declares `organization_entity` at `hasEntityPermission(`, so this is the same declaration for the same kind of target.

THE BOUNDARY IS A QUERY PREDICATE, NOT A FILTER AFTER AN UNSCOPED READ. For the postings route the `has_entity_permission` rpc is the predicate and it is the first thing that happens to the caller-named venue. For the review route the two boundaries are separate and both are server-side: `resolveHiringEntity(..., requirePermission: true)` runs canManageHiring, which really executes hasDirectEntityOwnership, the can_manage_hiring / has_perm / has_entity_permission rpcs and the legacy entity probes; and the service's read is `.eq('id').eq('employer_entity_type').eq('employer_entity_id')`. The suite's fake client honours `eq`/`in` against mutable stores, so a missing predicate produces a real cross-tenant write inside the fake rather than a theoretical one - proven by control C, where removing the route's permission check produced 'expected 200 to be 403' and the action really was called for the foreign venue.

THE ORGANIZATION COMES FROM THE VERIFIED ACTING CONTEXT, and this is the one place the task goes beyond simply naming a boundary. The review route still accepts a caller-named employer, because a hiring employer is polymorphic (venue / organization / artist) and `canManageHiring` is the canonical authority for it. But for the `organization` case the route now pins it: `resolveSchedulingOrgId({ supabase, employer })` accepts organizations.id, organizer_accounts.id or the owner user id and always returns organizations.id, which is the same identity space as `admin.orgId` (lib/auth/admin-context.ts:148, `organizationIdentityFromOrganizerAccount` maps `ops_org_id` to `organizationId`). A mismatch is a 403 and there is no fallback branch: the employer must resolve, and it must be the organization the verified acting context selected. CONTROL A removed exactly that block and the suite went red with 'AssertionError: expected \'approved\' to be \'uploaded\'' - the other tenant's document really was approved, with the state assertion reporting it before the status assertion.

FAIL CLOSED, verified rather than asserted. `resolveHiringEntity` returns a typed failure the route maps to 401/403/404/409/422/400 and returns on; there is no branch that reaches the service without a resolved, authorized employer. The acting context itself fails closed too: 'fails closed when the acting organization cannot be resolved at all' removes the `user_sessions` row and observes 409 `acting_context_required` with no write, and a signed-in user whose role does not carry the capability is refused with 403 `capability_denied`.

RESIDUAL, stated rather than absorbed. A `venue` employer is authorized by canManageHiring's per-venue probes, not by the acting organization, because resolveSchedulingOrgId returns null for venues and there is no DB-backed venue->organization ownership helper in this working set. So an Admin acting for org A who is separately a venue manager for venue B can still review venue B's onboarding documents from an org A session. That is a permission consequence, not an unscoped read, and closing it needs a canonical ownership decision plus a handoff; it is recorded rather than guessed at.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all three routes, all observed red. Control A (route A acting-organization binding removed): 2 failed, 'expected \'approved\' to be \'uploaded\'' plus the source assertion. Control B (route B reverted to `git show 16fb834f:app/api/admin/onboarding/enhanced-invite/route.ts`, sha256 cdcd5c1234c960d5e4ac169eefe9c8dfa3ce6afc37a888164b405b127498213a): 3 failed, 'expected 400 to be 401', 'expected 404 to be 401', and the shareToken source assertion - and the proof harness went red on 4 tests including '/api/admin/onboarding/enhanced-invite shareToken: expected false to be true'. Control C (route C's hasEntityPermission removed): 2 failed, 'expected 200 to be 403' plus the source assertion, and the proof harness went red with '/api/admin/staffing/job-postings hasEntityPermission(: expected false to be true'. Every file was restored from a byte-exact snapshot and sha256-verified, and the suite returned to 19/19 and 11/11.

NEGATIVE CONTROL D, the registry side: the three entries were reverted to legacy_pending_migration / none_recorded with the routes and the harness figures left as landed, and 5 proof tests went red - 'expected 243 to be 246' (the routeFiles-minus-none_recorded direction), 'expected 51 to be 48', 'expected \'legacy_pending_migration\' to be \'capability_gated\'', and the source-truth array carrying five named harness errors including 'declared none_recorded but the source contains acting_organization, organization_entity markers' and 'declared none_recorded but the source contains public_share markers'. Restored byte-exactly (sha256 1e41cfd2021cf0833232cff92d568a7e8a1dc2394a85c3c3c43eb63f7751ced7). This is the proof that the three boundaries cannot be satisfied by a registry edit, in either direction.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Unauthenticated requests to all three handlers are proven to receive 401.
evidence: All three are proven, and for two of them the 401 is a CHANGE: the postings route previously answered an unauthenticated caller with 400 (the `createJobPosting` action returns 'Not authenticated' and the route maps everything that is not 'Forbidden' to 400), and the invite route answered with 400 for an absent token and 404 for an unrecognised one.

PATCH /api/admin/onboarding/documents/[documentId]/review - 401 from withAuth via withAdminCapability. Asserted together with the exact production body `{ error: 'Unauthorized', details: 'Authentication required' }` and with the fact that nothing was read: no staff_documents query, no organizations lookup, no write, and the document store is still empty.

GET /api/admin/onboarding/enhanced-invite - 401 for an absent credential and for an unrecognised one. A bearer credential that is not presented, or is presented and does not match, is an authentication failure, which is also the correct HTTP semantics; 404 for an unknown token would have confirmed a token-existence oracle to a caller who already holds the token. The one client, app/onboarding/enhanced-onboarding-flow/page.tsx, branches on `data.success` and never on the status code, and always presents a token, so the change does not break the invite flow. The response body for the unrecognised case is asserted to contain neither the candidate id nor the position.
POST /api/admin/staffing/job-postings - 401 from withAuth, asserted with the same production body and with the fact that no job_posting_templates query was issued and the action was never called.

THE 401s ARE REAL, not a stubbed wrapper, and the suite is built to make that provable. `lib/auth/api-auth.ts` is not mocked: withAdminCapability -> withAuth -> authenticateApiRequest -> authenticateRequestWithBearerFallback -> resolveActingAdminContext -> requireAdminCapability all execute. `lib/auth/admin-context.ts` is not mocked either, so the user_sessions lookup, the organizer-account profile check, the active-membership check, the tour-collaborator fallback and the capabilities load really run. The only replacement is the Supabase transport, and its `auth.getUser()` is discriminating: with no token it resolves the configured session user, and with a token it resolves the bearer user only for one exact string, so a forged or wrong bearer cannot be waved through. Four independent anti-vacuity properties: (1) a positive test proves the same 401 path is not unconditional - with a RECOGNISED bearer token and NO cookie session the review route returns 200 and the document really is approved; (2) an unrecognised bearer with no session returns 401, so the 401 tracks the credential rather than the route; (3) a signed-in user with a `ticketing` role receives 403 `capability_denied`, which the 401 body could never produce, so the gate is a real decision; (4) each route has a source assertion naming the wrapper and the literal capability, so the gate cannot be deleted from the file while the behaviour tests are edited around it.

premises_that_turned_out_to_be_false: The dispatch stated all three handlers 'currently run on an implicit principal - withAdminAuth, which supplies only { user, supabase }'. FALSE. None of the three used withAdminAuth. All three were bare exported functions, which the ADMIN-016 analyzer classes `no_route_guard`, and they were three of the four members of the pinned noSourceGuardMethods set. GET enhanced-invite authenticated nobody at all - it is a share-token endpoint under app/api/admin/**. POST staffing/job-postings had no route-level guard; its only authorization lived inside the `createJobPosting` server action. PATCH documents/[documentId]/review used getAuthenticatedUserId from lib/api/hiring-route-helpers.ts plus a service-role client.
